### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**17** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 47 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **51** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ff99441d8c5155f14b602181337d43e41ec9b6a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `669e12769b71813fbe9c1d1c61d019b445c5a2f4` — the merge of head `dedc92d802c6ffe2099b8fe277b7467035fa06b4` into base `1ff99441d8c5155f14b602181337d43e41ec9b6a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 669e12769b71813fbe9c1d1c61d019b445c5a2f4 && git checkout 669e12769b71813fbe9c1d1c61d019b445c5a2f4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1ff99441d8c5155f14b602181337d43e41ec9b6a dedc92d802c6ffe2099b8fe277b7467035fa06b4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1ff99441d8c5155f14b602181337d43e41ec9b6a && git merge --no-ff dedc92d802c6ffe2099b8fe277b7467035fa06b4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ff99441d8c5155f14b602181337d43e41ec9b6a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set, `os serve` (and the `serve` child `os start` and `os dev` spawn — same `run()`).** A boot whose installed-plugin set holds a refused plugin now refuses unless the refusal is ruled out; before this head the refused plugin was printed and the boot went on for every code (the behaviour the #27123 integration file pinned, and the landed `47c3e12` changelog entry publishes as "non-fatal: the boot goes on"). The diff implies this narrowing and delivers it: the check at serve.ts 4795 reads `installedPluginsBoot?.refused ?? []`, sits right after `registerInstalledPlugins` (4794) and before `createHostCryptoProvider` (5143) and `runtime.start()` (5681), and is pinned by the new source-order case. The throw reaches the `run()` catch at 6096 (`restoreOutput`, `printError`, `this.exit(1)`); no inner catch sits between. Both the host branch and the standalone branch (closes at 2965, no return) reach 4794. **Right.**
2. **The ruled-out set.** (a) `runtime_undeclared` / `runtime_not_dispatched`: `checkRecord` reaches `dispatchPluginRuntime` only after the signature (step 3) and the tree (step 4) verified, so the tier is the verified artifact's own, and no boot of this CLI loads such a plugin in process. **Right.** (b) a refusal raised after the import whose `declaredServices` was read and lacks `crypto-provider`: `readDeclaredServices` reads `providesServices` under try/catch, `undefined` on a throw, string entries otherwise. **Right for an object.** (c) a non-object import (`export default 42`, a class): `readDeclaredServices` answers `[]` without reading anything, so the refusal is ruled out — while `refuseUnloadedCryptoProviderPlugins` refuses the same shape ("says nothing"). **Wrong** — ④ M2.
3. **Every other code refuses.** All pre-import codes of `InstalledPluginRefusalCode`, `import_failed` (pushed before any read, so `declaredServices` is absent), a post-import refusal whose read threw, `plugin_name_taken` / `kernel_refused` carrying the loaded entry's declaration, and `loader_failed` / `records_unreadable` (ids `*` / `?`, no disable remedy). **Right.** A disabled plugin lands in `disabled`, never in `refused`. **Right.**
4. **Public surface, `@objectstack/runtime`.** `InstalledPluginRefusal.declaredServices?: string[]` and `LoadedInstalledPlugin.declaredServices?: string[]`, both exported from the package root (index.ts 90, 94). Additive, optional, set only when read. **Right**, and a widening of the published surface — ②.
5. **`registerInstalledPlugins`.** A refusal it raises copies the loaded entry's `declaredServices` when present (`withDeclaredServices`), including `[]`. **Right.**
6. **The refusal text.** Names each stopping plugin as `id@version (code)`, the service by name, and `os plugin disable ID` once per named id (deduplicated); ruled-out refusals are not named; the `*` / `?` entries get the "could not be read" label and no disable remedy. **Right**, with the remedy claim narrowed in ④ S1.
7. **Metadata protocol.** No key an author writes moves; `providesServices` is ADR-0116's existing field, read, not changed. `Metadata-protocol: none` **right**; both packages `patch` **right** under ruling A on #25105.
8. **The #27123 integration file.** Re-pinned as: a refused boot first (exit non-zero, no `Migration complete`, both stopping plugins named with their disable remedies, the sandbox-tier refusal printed but not named as a reason, no installed plugin's `init` ran), then `os plugin disable` of both and the file's original two boots. The re-pin matches the tree. **Right** as a pin; it is also the published behaviour this PR reverses, which is ②'s subject.

### ② Semver level

**Ruling on the `Clause-②:` line: `yes (narrowing)`. The PR body and the changeset say `no`. Must-fix M1.**

- The arm. Clause ② asks whether the card widens the accept set or the public surface, and the `(narrowing)` arm flags an accept-set narrowing (AGENTS.md Post-Task 3; `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` signal 4, #16421: "an accept-set narrowing is exactly the change a consumer needs told about"). This diff narrows the accept set of `os serve`: an installed-plugin set the command booted on `main` — one holding a plugin refused as `tree_changed`, `signature_key_untrusted`, `manifest_invalid`, `import_failed` or any other non-ruled-out code — is refused on this head. That behaviour was delivered and published: the #27123 integration pins read "refused … and boots on", and the landed `47c3e12` entry in packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md states of the boot-time loader's refusal "It stays non-fatal: the boot goes on and every other installed plugin loads." An operator upgrading with such a refusal in place sees a boot stop where it ran; the release notes must route that entry to the manual-handling section, which only the arm (or a BREAKING banner) does.
- Why not `no`, as ⑧ (#31263) and ⑧A (#31320) carried. ⑧A refused a shape the package never delivered (a bare config's string entries were never loaded), and ⑧ made an undocumented tolerance loud (the stack loop's error swallow, carried by a code comment). Neither reversed a published consumer-facing statement. This PR does: the loader's non-fatal refusal was published in the changelog and pinned as product behaviour. The distinction leaves the two stock changesets as declared; the seat may still route series-wide uniformity to the maintainer.
- Why `yes` rather than `no (narrowing)`: two optional fields on two types exported from `@objectstack/runtime`'s root entry enlarge the published surface — the widening half of the question. `yes (narrowing)` is a legal spelling (`clause2-line.mjs`; landed precedents `47c3e12`, `a9f654e`).
- What the changeset must carry (AGENTS.md Post-Task 3): the arm on the `Clause-②:` line in the changeset body and the PR body; the ADR-0087 disposition comment (`check:adr-0087-registration` judges a newly added changeset whose arm reads `narrowing`; the closest landed shape is `47c3e12`'s `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — no key, export or stored shape is removed or renamed; the remedy is an operator's act); a BREAKING banner naming the accept-set narrowing at `os serve` (and the `serve` child of `os start` / `os dev`); and the before / now / remedy the body already half-states. **The level does not move**: under ruling A the level follows the metadata protocol alone, and `Metadata-protocol: none` keeps `@objectstack/cli: patch` and `@objectstack/runtime: patch` — `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` accepts a `(narrowing)` arm beside `none` at `patch`.
- Disclosure. Read: the PR title and body (both languages), the commit message, the changeset, the new function's docblock and call-site comment, the refusal string, the loader's two field docblocks and `readDeclaredServices`, the boot helper's header, and the three test files' headers and case names. Each states which refusals are refused, which are ruled out, where the check sits and what the refusal names — the level the PR body uses — and the maintainer's why line verbatim. The refusal's "seals every secret field, datasource credential and encrypted setting, so this boot does not choose another one" is the sentence already on `main` in `refuseUnloadedCryptoProviderPlugins`. **No breach.**

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Two hand-back items outside this PR's scope.** Read against the tree and confirmed; under the disclosure ruling they are carried as private items, not described here. Not this PR's scope.
2. **PR body "Not measured: a real crypto-provider plugin installed and refused end to end."** The declaration branch is pinned at the function (four codes × four declarations) and at the loader (five cases); the integration file refuses with a plain node plugin and pins that no `init` ran. Accepted on this head; the end-to-end case belongs with the series' acceptance run, not this PR.
3. **Hand-back "Clause-②: no … Seat judges."** Ruled in ② — M1.
4. **Hand-back "pushes after #31396 lands."** The head's merge-base `ae816c40b` is on `main`; the PR body's "one commit on main" reads true.
5. **Dev flag, implicit: the remedy `os plugin disable ID` is how a boot goes on without a refused plugin** (docblock and changeset). Not true for four codes — ④ S1.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing itself, read against the published spec on `main`.** The capability consumers hold is the one `packages/types/src/crypto-provider-service.ts` publishes: a plugin that declares `crypto-provider` in `providesServices` is the host's one provider, handed to everything that seals a secret. "A refused installed plugin is printed and the boot goes on" (the loader's header on `main`, the #27123 pins, `47c3e12`) is a tolerance of the loader, not a capability a consumer builds on — and where the refused plugin is the provider, the tolerance defeats the published capability at the very consumer that chooses the provider. The PR does not narrow at a consumer what the spec grants; it makes the host's own composition contract real where it was inert, by the same rule `refuseUnloadedCryptoProviderPlugins` already applies to the stack's `plugins` on `main` (⑧). The rule-outs are the right ones: a tier verdict is taken only on a verified artifact, and a declaration is trusted only when it was read. The remedy routes the operator to an explicit act (`os plugin disable`). The capability is neither taken away nor narrowed at the consumer; it is enforced. ADR-0049's "parsed, unmarked, silently inert" state is left for exactly one shape — M2.

Break attempts, each against the tree: every code of `InstalledPluginRefusalCode` and which arm it takes (① 2–3); a post-import refusal whose read threw (absent, refused); a plugin refused before its import (absent, refused); `import_failed` (absent, refused); a loaded plugin that declares the provider and fails `kernel.use` or has its name taken (carried, refused); the loader throwing outright and the records file unreadable (refused, no disable remedy); a disabled plugin (`disabled`, not a refusal); the order against `registerInstalledPlugins`, `createHostCryptoProvider` and `runtime.start()` (① 1); `os start` and `os dev` (the `serve` child, same path); the standalone branch (reaches the check); a bundle object without `init` (wrapped into `AppPlugin`, whose own declaration is read — a bundle registers no service, so no exposure); the remedy text (S1); a non-object import (M2).

- **M2 (must-fix) — a non-object import is ruled out though nothing of it was read.** `readDeclaredServices` (installed-plugin-loader.ts 165) answers `[]` for a value that is not an object or function, and reads a static field off a function; `inspectImported` refuses both as `not_a_plugin`. So an installed plugin whose entry evaluates to `42`, a string, `undefined` (a factory that answered nothing) or a class carries `declaredServices: []` and `refuseRefusedInstalledCryptoProviderPlugins` rules it out — the loader test row "refused after its import, not an object" pins that as intended. The rule the PR declares it follows, `refuseUnloadedCryptoProviderPlugins`, refuses the same materialization: `said` is `undefined` when `materialized` is not an object, and "an entry that never materialized says nothing, and is refused". The PR body's "whose `providesServices` could be read" is not true of a value that has none to read. Fix: `readDeclaredServices` answers `undefined` (nothing read) for a non-object, matching ⑧'s `typeof === 'object'` test — one line — and the loader test's "not an object" row expects the field absent; the function-level case "a plugin refused after its import is judged by what it declares" needs no change. With that, every post-import refusal is judged by a declaration that was read, or refused.
- **S1 (should-fix) — the remedy names `os plugin disable ID` for four codes it does not help.** `verifyInstalledPlugins` checks `install_dir_unexpected` before the disabled set, so a plugin disabled for that code is refused again at the next boot and the boot refuses again; `uninstall_failed` and `record_changed` are uninstall-pending records, which `os plugin disable` refuses (`findPluginInstallation` → `plugin_uninstall_pending`); `disabled_state_unreadable` is a disable-state file the command cannot read either (`disable_state_failed`). The refusal stays fail-closed, and its first clause ("Fix what refused it") holds. Fix in the refusal text (name `os plugin uninstall ID`, or the record, for those codes), or in the loader (honour the disabled set before the directory check); the docblock's "`os plugin disable` is how a boot goes on without one" follows the choice.
- Nit — `readDeclaredServices(plugin)` is computed in both arms of the load loop; one read above the `if (refusal)` serves both. No effect on correctness.
